name: global-equity-etf/global-etf-sleeve-blend
title: Global-ETF sleeve blend — US-vs-ROW relative trend + FOMC global beta
description: Equal-risk blend of two uncorrelated country-ETF edges: 0.67 × a slow (126/252/504d) sign trend on each country's SPY-beta-hedged spread and on the EW ex-US aggregate (market-neutral, 10 % vol, rebalanced on the last NYSE session of each month), plus 0.87 × a long equal-weight country basket held over FOMC day −1 and day 0 only.
direction: long/short basket, near market-neutral (average net +0.035; gross avg 1.41, max 3.00)

backtest.cost_type: 5 bp/side on country ETFs, 1 bp/side on SPY, charged on |dw|; price (auto-adjusted) returns, no financing on cash or leverage

live_notes: SIM book: filled at the yfinance daily close from the shared data/ cache, with no order book, rejection or partial fill, and no margin interest on levered days. Weaker evidence than a venue fill -- do not read this track as exchange-cleared.

Cost: the research charges 5 bp/side on the country ETFs and 1 bp on SPY; SimPortfolioBroker takes one rate, so the daemon is built as 1 bp slippage + 4 bp fee = 5 bp on all ten legs (conservative by 4 bp on the SPY hedge). Report ladder: 2 bp -> 0.87, 5 bp -> 0.81, 10 bp -> 0.72 full-sample. NOTE: live_lib.broker_from_meta (the dashboard's flatten button) rebuilds a basket with the 1 bp / 10 bp defaults; that affects a one-off flatten only, not the daemon.
Gross cap 3.1 per spec (max observed 3.00, 99th pct 2.31) -- a backstop that should never bind; if the journal shows scaled_by, the book is outside what the research tested.

Calendar upkeep: code/global-equity-etf/shared/trading_calendar.py:NYSE_HOLIDAYS covers 2026-27 and code/global-equity-etf/fomc-global-beta/fomc_snapshot.csv runs to 2027-12-08. Extend both each year (the runner logs a warning within 90 days of either end); past them, month-ends and FOMC windows next to holidays are mis-timed.

Risks the report names: the trend sleeve is a bet on multi-year US-vs-ex-US regimes and loses at each flip (2002, 2010-11, 2023, 2025); the FOMC sleeve's P&L is concentrated (top 5 of 205 meetings = 55 %). A +1-day lag drops the blend to 0.64 because it moves the FOMC window onto days 0/+1 -- the daemon must trade the close the signal is computed on.

Selection: ~230 book configurations tried in the session; DSR 0.95 at N = 100. The slow trend lookback was chosen after seeing the ETF era; the independent 1980-2000 backcast (0.52) is the check on it.

Timing: row t of target_weights is held close_t -> close_{t+1}. The daemon wakes 00:00:20 UTC and trades only when the bar all 10 legs agree on changes; a forming bar during US hours raises instead of trading, and any leg lagging SPY's bar blocks the rebalance.

Deploy check 2026-09-26: runner --check on bar 2026-09-25 equals strategy.target_weights recomputed over the research panel exactly (max|diff| 0.0): gross 1.304, net -0.192; largest legs SPY -0.370, INDA -0.177, EWA -0.161, EWC +0.146 (trend sleeve set 2026-08-31, FOMC sleeve off; next window opens at the 2026-10-26 close). The research's spec_weights.parquet matches the recompute at lag 0 (max|diff| 1.7e-5 over 6997 rows; lag 1 max 1.95), i.e. it stores decision-time weights.
